radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane.description: Major-radius coordinate of a magnetic flux surface at the outboard midplane, locating its position relative to the toroidal symmetry axis. The value at magnetic-axis height coincides with the surface's maximum-major-radius location only for an up-down-symmetric equilibrium.
radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate at outboard midplane

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ satisfying $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, the major-radius coordinate is related to horizontal Cartesian coordinates by:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

Here $R$ is the [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) measured from the toroidal symmetry axis; $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, with zero set by the facility convention; and $Z$ is vertical height. The values $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the evaluated point in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, whose origin lies on the toroidal symmetry axis and for which $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

The quantity applies separately to each magnetic flux surface identified by the poloidal magnetic-flux function $\psi$, which labels the surface; it is a point value, not a flux-surface average. It is evaluated at the vertical height of the magnetic axis. In an up-down-symmetric equilibrium, that height coincides with the height of the surface's outboard-midplane point of maximum major radius. In an up-down-asymmetric equilibrium, the maximum-major-radius point lies at another height, so the value at magnetic-axis height is not the surface maximum. This value is distinct from the [radial coordinate at the inboard midplane](name:radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane), which locates the inboard-side position.

This is a locus-specific instance of the general [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), evaluated at the outboard-midplane locus.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_m.description: Signed major-radius separation between a measurement position mapped along its flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix there; positive values are on the scrape-off-layer side.
radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_m.documentation:
This quantity is the signed separation along the [major-radius direction] between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the [outboard midplane] and the separatrix at that locus.

The separation is the mapped position's major radius minus the major radius of the separatrix intersection:

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}} = R_{\mathrm{map,mid}} - R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}
$$

where $\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the mapped separatrix separation, $R_{\mathrm{map,mid}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the mapped measurement position, and $R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the [separatrix intersection at the outboard midplane]. The latter two coordinates are instances of [radial coordinate at outboard midplane](name:radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane).

Flux-surface mapping preserves the measurement position's flux-surface label. This is a major-radius separation, not the shortest geometric distance to the separatrix or a local flux-surface-normal separation; it is zero at the separatrix and negative for mapped positions inside it. For a separatrix-bounded plasma, the reference radius is the outboard-midplane value of the [radial plasma-boundary outline](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the mapped measurement position lies outside the separatrix in the scrape-off layer, at greater major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane.description: Major-radius coordinate of the low-field-side intersection between a magnetic flux surface and the equatorial midplane.
radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the point where a specified magnetic flux surface intersects the equatorial midplane on its outboard, low-field side. It gives the outboard radial extent of that surface rather than a distance across the plasma or an average over the surface.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with unit-vector basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, the major-radius coordinate is related to the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ by:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

Here $R$ is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, and $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates measured from that axis.

The quantity applies to one specified magnetic flux surface, identified by its poloidal magnetic-flux label $\psi$, where $\psi$ denotes the flux function labeling nested magnetic surfaces. It is evaluated only at the outboard intersection with the equatorial midplane; it excludes the inboard intersection and any flux-surface average.

It is a locus-specific specialization of the [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), obtained by evaluating $R$ at the outboard midplane. The corresponding [inboard-midplane radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane) describes the distinct high-field-side intersection of the same type of magnetic surface.

radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_m.description: Signed major-radius offset from the magnetic separatrix after a measurement position is mapped along its flux surface to the outboard midplane, positive in the scrape-off layer.
radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_m.documentation:
This quantity is the signed major-radius separation between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix at that locus.

The defining relation is

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}} = R_{\mathrm{map,mid}} - R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}
$$

where $\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the mapped separatrix separation, $R_{\mathrm{map,mid}}$ is the major radius of the mapped measurement position, and $R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the major radius of the separatrix intersection at the outboard midplane. Major radius is measured from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The mapping preserves the measurement position's flux-surface label. The result is not the shortest geometric distance to the separatrix or a local flux-surface-normal separation. It vanishes on the separatrix and is negative for mapped positions inside it. For a separatrix-bounded plasma, the reference radius is the outboard-midplane value of the [radial plasma-boundary outline](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the mapped measurement position lies outside the separatrix in the scrape-off layer, at greater major radius than the separatrix intersection.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: points at the midplane height with major radius greater than the magnetic-axis radius. The data's midplane identifier selects that height, or it is the magnetic-axis height when none is given. For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $Z = Z_{\mathrm{mid}},\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $Z_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the midplane height the data's midplane identifier selects, the magnetic-axis height when none is given; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

Docked for template drift versus the accepted counterpart radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane, which opens with 'Major radius coordinate R of the inboard (high-field-side) midplane intersection of a magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame'; the candidate omits the frame and the explicit R token and uses a slightly different intersection phrasing. Documentation quality (17/20): Strong normative body—defining equation R_out(ψ)=R(x_out(ψ)), symbols glossed, cylindrical frame, outboard-only scope clause, and a working name: link to the inboard counterpart.
